 NEC Nijmegen beat Dinamo Zagreb 4-2 for first UEFA Europa League win 
 Thursday, 22 October 2026 - 21:01
 NEC Nijmegen gained a vital victory on Thursday in the UEFA Europa League. Dick Schreuder’s side defeated Dinamo Zagreb 4-2 in the Maksimir stadium. Team captain Tjarron Chery got two goals, with Bryan Linssen and Clement Bischoff accounting for the other two.
 It is NEC’s first win in the competition this season. Prior to this, they had been hammered by Juventus and drew with Levski Sofia at home. 
 NEC were inches from going behind in the 19th minute. Luka Stojkovic chipped the ball over the onrushing NEC keeper Gonzalo Crettaz, but center back Ahmetcan Kaplan was able to clear the ball in an acrobatic manner. 
 Next up it was Schreuder’s team’s turn to come close to breaking the deadlock. Noe Lebreton’s effort from around 25 meters hit the crossbar before going out for a goal kick. 
 And it was NEC who took the lead in Zagreb in the 25th minute. A great pass from Perr Schuurs found Tobias Storm on the wing; his low cross made its way through the box to Clement Bischoff, who kept his cool with the finish. 
 The home side equalized seven minutes later. A hanging cross from Matteo Perez Vinlof was perfect for the side’s 1.95-meter-tall striker, Dion Drena Beljo, who nodded the ball under Crettaz. 
 It seemed like the second followed a few minutes later when former Feyenoord midfielder Luka Ivanusec found the net, but the goal was disallowed due to Beljo being in an offside position.
 But as has often been the case this season, NEC did not heed the warning and conceded shortly after this. Stojkovic found acres of space outside NEC’s penalty area and played a pass to Beljo, who was left unmarked at the far corner of the box. His first effort was saved by Crettaz, but the rebound went right back to the striker for the easiest of goals.
 However, NEC fought back to equalize before halftime. Bischoff added an assist to his goal with a cross that actually went behind striker Bryan Linssen, but the veteran did extremely well to arch the header into the net. 
 Linssen scored the half-chance and then missed a much easier one a minute later. A long ball from Crettaz was misjudged by Sergi Dominguez and came through for Linssen, but his volley towards goal went comfortably wide. 
 NEC took the lead in the 54th minute. Linssen played a low pass to Chery, who was running into the box. The Suriname international got the slightest of touches on the ball with the bottom of his studs, which was just about enough to push it past goalkeeper Dominik Kotarski. 
 Crettaz kept his team ahead with a double save in the 73rd minute. First, he got down low to stop Dinamo captain Josip Misic from scoring before also blocking the rebound by Mislav Orsic.
 This proved vital as NEC got their fourth seven minutes later. Chery stepped up for the side, with a lovely lofted effort into the far corner.
